deprecation_note: Project-level model routing is retired. The user-global policy at ~/.agents/skills/orca-model-routing/routing.json is authoritative. This file is retained for audit only.

model_id_policy.verification: Compare launch.requested with launch.effective for every attempt. A declared fallback may change the model; an undeclared replacement is an infrastructure failure.

coordinator.purpose: Create the Run and tasks, dispatch workers, wait for settlements, route findings, and release terminals.

triage.purpose: Classify issues, detect duplicates, identify affected areas, and flag owner-decision or high-risk work.

planner.purpose: For complex work: reproduce, propose root cause, define file ownership, tests, and a bounded implementation plan.

developer.purpose: Implement scoped bugs and features, add regression tests, run required checks, commit, and open the PR.

developer_complex.purpose: Implement cross-module, SQL, permission, migration, or contract-sensitive changes after the planner handoff.

reviewer.purpose: Independent read-only review of the diff, issue acceptance, regression validity, and deployment risk.

escalation.purpose: Resolve architecture, data-loss, security, repeated-review-blocker, or owner-red-line questions. Output analysis only.

release.purpose: Merge and deploy only after required CI checks are green, using the existing blue-green workflow.

use_planner: the issue crosses more than two runtime modules
the root cause is not reproduced after two focused attempts
the change touches SQL joins, migrations, permissions, or data deletion
the change affects Flask, templates, MCP, and persistence contracts together
use_escalation: review returns two blockers of the same class
a production data-loss or security risk is possible
an owner red line or product semantic decision is required
high effort has failed twice without new evidence
hard_gates: one worktree has only one code writer at a time
reviewers never edit the reviewed worktree
nested agents may perform read-only exploration unless explicitly authorized
CI, merge, and deployment remain deterministic and outside model discretion
